image_description: A close-up view of a Nile crocodile's head and upper snout emerging from water covered in dense green duckweed. The crocodile is facing left, with its mouth slightly open revealing large conical teeth. The skin texture is rough and armored with visible osteoderms. One eye is clearly visible, positioned dorsally.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers to a point consistent with the V-shape of a crocodile, distinct from the U-shape of an alligator. The head structure appears broad and robust.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Large, yellowish conical teeth are clearly visible along the jawline. The fourth tooth on the lower jaw appears to fit into the upper jaw notch, a key diagnostic feature.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is positioned on top of the skull. While the pupil shape is hard to resolve at this resolution, the dorsal positioning is correct. No obvious artifact in the eye structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Nostrils are visible at the anterior end of the snout, consistent with anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and neck are visible; the full body length cannot be verified due to framing/occlusion by water plants.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin behind the eyes and on the neck shows heavy, irregular armor plating consistent with osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is greyish-brown and the texture is highly detailed and rough, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside of the crocodile is submerged or occluded by the angle; ventral scales are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are completely submerged or out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is not visible in the image.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The green duckweed has a slightly repetitive, 'stamped' pattern in some areas, lacking individual leaf variation. It blends into the snout edge with slight softness, suggesting minor generation blur or texture synthesis issues.

The transition between the teeth and the gum/lip area is somewhat muddy. Some teeth appear to merge slightly with the jawbone rather than sitting in distinct sockets, a common AI artifact in complex dental structures.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the species classification as Nile Crocodile vs other crocodilians based on snout shape and scale pattern.
To check for edge bleeding or fusion between the hard scales of the snout and the soft organic matter of the duckweed.
To assess overall realism, lighting consistency, and detect subtle texture anomalies in the skin and water.

focus_areas: Tooth socket definition and separation from gums
Edge sharpness between crocodile skin and floating vegetation
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the teeth. AI often struggles with interlocking teeth, causing them to melt into the jaw or each other. Verify if the fourth lower tooth actually fits into the upper jaw notch as described in taxonomy. Also, scrutinize the duckweed texture for repetition artifacts.

metadata.class_label: African crocodile, Nile crocodile, Crocodylus niloticus
